text: A systematic review identified 59 rigorous evaluations of clinical guidelines: 24 addressed specific clinical conditions, 27 preventive care, and 8 prescribing or support services. All but 4 studies detected significant improvements in the process of care after guidelines were introduced, and all but 2 of the 11 studies assessing care outcomes reported significant improvements. The authors conclude that explicit guidelines do improve clinical practice when introduced within rigorous evaluations, though the magnitude of performance improvements varied considerably.
